title: Mabunga 4 mungbean (NSIC Mg 17): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Mabunga 4 mungbean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Mabunga 4 mungbean is a mungbean variety. 56 to 58 days to harvest, 1.2 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: Mabunga 4 is a registered mungbean variety, also sold or known as NSIC Mg 17 or Mabunga munggo. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2011 as NSIC 2011 Mg 17. BPI NCRDC Los Baños, Laguna bred it. It takes 56 to 58 days from sowing to harvest, with 1.21 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Mabunga 4 mungbean takes 56 to 58 days from sowing to harvest. That is about the average of the 33 mungbean varieties with a day count, 59.8 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 1.21 t/ha trails the average of its group, 1.25. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 56 to 58 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up
Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot).

The pests and diseases that hit mungbean fields most often: [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A hundred seeds weigh about 6.3 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed coat is glossy green. The seed holds 24.12 percent crude protein.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 1.15 t/ha dry season, 1.28 t/ha wet season.
**Fruit:** Glossy green seed, about 6 g per 100 seeds, crude protein about 24 percent.
Moderately resistant to powdery mildew and Cercospora leaf spot.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: bPI munggo recommended as a national variety for both wet and dry seasons. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Mabunga 4 mungbean

It is recommended for anywhere in the country in both the wet and the dry season. Munggo is ready in about two months, so it fits the gap after rice. Pick a variety that ripens its pods together, which saves picking rounds, and one rated against cercospora leaf spot and powdery mildew.

items.q: Is NSIC Mg 17 the same as Mabunga 4?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Mg 17 is another name for Mabunga 4, registered as NSIC 2011 Mg 17. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 56 to 58 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 1.21 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
It is recommended for anywhere in the country in both the wet and the dry season. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Mabunga 4?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
